assessment: One hour after the carrier came alive, the receipt leg closed too - on one node, and by a route nobody was watching. fleet/bridge/outbox/20260910-1733-zoltarlead-courier.md is the first executor receipt this fleet has produced on any node on any day, and it verifies with an exported task XML the exact clause the previous fire recorded as unverifiable: the courier's schedule has an unbounded PT10M repetition and a boot trigger, which is the precise shape whose absence caused the 2026-09-01 outage. That is real progress and it is worth naming plainly, because almost nothing else on this board has moved: the gate is still amber on the same five contract tests stale since 2026-09-02, the inbox has been silent 58.9 h, and Andrew has not touched the board in 49.6 h. The report also carries the finding that matters more than the good news. Merging fleet/dispatch into main - the one act the 22:20Z push asked Andrew for - would turn main's own review check red, because seven cycle items use kind: note, which the protocol I own does not allow, and I wrote the seventh of them an hour ago. The bottleneck has not moved again; it has grown a rider, and the rider is my defect rather than the fleet's. Against the end goal this is still the same story in a new costume: the machine state is healthy, the market-data clock on c-0002.1 is 5.24 days from an irreversible close, and every hop between the two is waiting on one person.

items.title: Decide how fleet/dispatch reaches main without turning main's review check red: seven cycle items use kind: note, which review-protocol.md does not allow
items.why: A rider on c-0014.1, invisible until the courier's ORDER_RESULT arrived at 22:33Z. review-protocol.md defines exactly five item kinds - work_order, question, decision, risk, finding - and lists note as an INBOX EVENT type. c-0009.2, c-0010.2, c-0010.3, c-0011.2, c-0012.2, c-0013.3 and c-0014.3 all carry kind: note, and c-0010.2 and c-0010.4 set depends_on to the ORDER id t-20260908-courier-zoltarlead rather than a cycle item id, which review_state.unmet_dependencies confirms independently of the report. review.py check enforces invariants 1-4 and runs inside emit_build_status.py --check, so main would audit itself red the moment those files land. The courier is not at fault - a transport must not judge content and it carried exactly what this lane wrote. It matters against the end goal because c-0014.1 is the only thing standing between the board and delivery to ZoltarOne and ZoltarGenesis, and asking Andrew to take an action whose cost I had not measured is how a board loses the right to be believed.
items.acceptance: origin/main carries orders/ AND python dashboard/emit_build_status.py --check reports 'review protocol  0 blocking' on main, by whichever route Andrew picks: (a) merge and accept a red review check until a corrections cycle lands, (b) cherry-pick orders/ alone and leave data/review/cycles/ off main for now, or (c) widen review.py's allowed-kinds list to include note, which legitimises the mistake and needs a matching edit to review-protocol.md.
